text: Azure SQL Database offers two purchasing models, DTU and vCore, each with its own service tiers. Both answer the same question — how much compute, memory, and I/O — with different units and different control.

The DTU model bundles compute, memory, and I/O into Basic, Standard, and Premium. The vCore model prices compute and storage separately across General Purpose, Business Critical, and Hyperscale — and is required for Azure Hybrid Benefit.

Within vCore, you also pick a compute option — provisioned, fixed and always billed, or serverless, auto-scaling and billed per second. Picking a tier is really at least two decisions, sometimes three.
Lesson 9 takes DTU vs. vCore all the way; Lesson 10 takes provisioned vs. serverless the same way. Next up: DTU vs. vCore in full.
